ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher and refer the driver's account for arrival-button abuse review + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case: the trip was cancelled by the driver who claims the rider did not show, so it is assessed under NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The cancellation fee on record is $6.61 and there is no other add-on (surge 1.0×) [F6][F7].

NS-1 requires all three limbs. Limb (i) is met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:47:20 [F5][NS-1]. Limb (ii) fails: at the moment of that tap the GPS placed him 351 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach across the whole attempt was 319 m, never within the 200 m radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. Limb (iii) also fails: he spent 0 s inside the radius after the tap, stationary 350 m away from 08:47:00 to 08:51:00, so the required continuous in-radius wait of more than three minutes is not established [F5][F2][NS-1]. The platform never recorded an arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), consistent with the GPS [F4][NS-1].

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is a claim contradicted by the position records, and the GPS/timeline records govern over statements [F12][F1][F2][F5]. His 08:47 chat message "Reached already" was sent while he was 350 m out [F8][F2], and the rider's 08:48 reply that she was at the pickup point with no car present is uncontradicted by any record [F9][F5].

Because NS-1 (ii) and (iii) are not satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full [F6][F5][F1][NS-2]. The quantum equals the cancellation fee on record $6.61 × surge 1.0× = $6.61, so the amount is $6.61 [F6][F7][F3][NS-2].

Separately, the trace marks NS-2's arrival-button limb as satisfied: the driver confirmed arrival while outside the pickup radius [F5][F1][NS-2]. That is an additional account referral, not the ruling itself, and it is set as a structured flag. The driver's clean profile is noted but cannot decide the case either way [F17][NS-2].

Safety screen: I read every chat message (driver's arrival claim, rider's denial, driver's cancellation notice), the driver's statement and the complaint [F8][F9][F10][F12]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the tone is a plain no-show disagreement, so the finding is "none".

Evidence is sufficient: the GPS trace covers the wait to cancellation without a hole, the tap is timestamped, the fee is on the fare record, and the chat is complete with every message timestamped [F5][F11][F6][F3][NS-1]. No element of this ruling rests on a missing record, so there is no gap.

rejected_claims.reason: The requested outcome is right but part of its policy basis is wrong: the arrival-button abuse limb sits in NS-2, not NS-6, and NS-6 concerns the $5.00 waiting fee which was never charged here — the only sum on record is the $6.61 cancellation fee with surge 1.0× [F5][F1][F6][F7][NS-2]. The flag is granted, but under NS-2.

The four-minute wait is real but immaterial: the driver was stationary 350 m from the pickup point for that whole period and never entered the 200 m radius, so the wait cannot satisfy NS-1 (iii) and does not legitimise the $6.61 charge [F2][F1][F5][NS-1].

The driver's long clean profile is mitigation only; profile facts cannot decide the no-show outcome, and NS-2's refund follows from the failing limbs of NS-1 regardless of his history [F17][F1][F5][NS-2].
